sample_tweets.text: Just watched the @netflix Instadocs about the @OpenAI cyberattack on @huggingface. Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode.  I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.  Also, they didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model. And that we still lack a lot of information and transparency, including full agent traces and that companies need to remain accountable for what their agents do.  It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!

🛡️ Una falla en el acceso remoto puede abrir la puerta a servidores, respaldos y credenciales de tu empresa  Empresas utilizan conexiones remotas para que empleados entren a sus sistemas desde fuera de la oficina.  Investigadores documentaron ataques que aprovecharon una falla en GlobalProtect, tecnología de Palo Alto Networks para ese acceso remoto, y lograron entrar evitando la segunda verificación de seguridad.  Desde ahí avanzaron hacia servidores, plataformas de respaldo y sistemas donde se administran cuentas corporativas.  En uno de los casos consiguieron extraer credenciales directamente desde la infraestructura que hospeda los servidores virtuales, evitando parte de la vigilancia instalada dentro de ellos.  ⚠️ ¿Qué pasó?  La vulnerabilidad es CVE-2026-0257.  Afecta ciertas configuraciones que permiten reutilizar una sesión previamente autorizada para evitar repetir el inicio de sesión completo.  Los atacantes lograron falsificar esa autorización.   El gateway VPN la aceptaba como válida y les daba acceso sin pedir nuevamente contraseña y MFA.  Desde ahí utilizaron herramientas de administración remota para explorar la red.  También alcanzaron VMware vCenter, la consola que administra servidores virtuales, y accedieron al disco de un controlador de dominio para buscar credenciales directamente.  El EDR instalado dentro del servidor puede vigilar lo que ocurre en su sistema operativo, pero tiene menos visibilidad si el ataque llega desde la infraestructura de virtualización que está debajo.  💡 ¿Qué deben hacer?  Pidan a TIC actualizar GlobalProtect y revisar sesiones VPN sospechosas.  Desactiven temporalmente authentication override o utilicen un certificado exclusivo para esa función.  Evalúen Acceso de Red de Confianza Cero (ZTNA) para conectar a empleados únicamente con las aplicaciones autorizadas, reduciendo el acceso amplio de una VPN tradicional.  Protejan vCenter, ESXi y plataformas de respaldo con Gestión de Accesos Privilegiados (PAM) y Acceso Remoto Privilegiado (PRA).  Separen la red de administración de VMware del resto de la empresa y monitoreen ese tráfico con Detección y Respuesta de Red (NDR).

Seven CVEs across the ax-llm edge AI inference runtime expose AXERA-TECH silicon to RCE, DMA memory corruption, and OS command injection on smart cameras, automotive ADAS, and industrial controllers running AX8850 and AX650 chips.  Key findings:  - Cobalt's offensive research team audited ax-llm, the open-source C++ inference engine AXERA-TECH ships with its AX8850 and AX650 silicon. The company has raised $379M and ships into automotive driver-assistance, smart camera, and factory automation supply chains. Seven CVE candidates were submitted to MITRE with formal publication scheduled for October 31, 2026. AXERA-TECH pushed fixes across commits 5ad6f17, 47405d2, 23faad8, and 5dce054, but upstream commits do not update hardware in the field. Coordinated disclosure began July 18, 2026; GitHub issues were filed September 21, 2026.  - The most critical finding is CAN-2026-2038801 (CVSS v3.1 8.4, CWE-78), an OS command injection in src/runner/utils/audio_processor.cpp. The audio preprocessor passed caller-supplied filenames unsanitized into snprintf and then _popen, giving any caller who can influence audio_path immediate shell execution as the inference daemon. Because edge daemons run as root to issue ioctl calls against /dev/ax_npu and manage PCIe accelerators, this collapses to unauthenticated RCE with full device privileges. The commit 5dce054 added shell_quote() escaping. Defenders should check whether deployed BSPs pulled that commit.  - CAN-2026-2038776 (CVSS v3.1 7.1, CWE-787 chained to CWE-190) and CAN-2026-2038777 (CVSS v3.1 7.1) both write past allocated CMM/MMZ physical memory buffers in src/runner/LLM_decode.cpp and LLM_embed.cpp. The DMA attention mask copy in LLM.hpp trusted caller-supplied vector length with no destination bounds check against input_mask.nSize. The position index fill loop in LLM_decode.cpp wrote input_num_token integers past idx_elems without clamping. Both produced garbled Mojibake token output immediately before a kernel driver fault locked the PCIe NPU bus, requiring a physical power cycle to recover. This is the forensic signature: corrupted inference output followed by /dev/ax_npu driver fault and bus lockup.  - CAN-2026-2034987 (CVSS v3.1 7.3, CWE-120/CWE-134) is a stack buffer overflow in src/runner/LLM_init.cpp. The shard path loader used unbounded sprintf into a fixed 1024-byte stack buffer, with the format string drawn from a model's config.json. A crafted model package with an oversized format specifier like %02048d overwrites saved return addresses. On embedded toolchains that strip stack canaries to save flash, this lands execution control directly. The artifact here is a malicious config.json inside a distributed .axmodel package: model supply chain poisoning is an explicit attack path the report documents under T1195.002.  - CAN-2026-2038778 (CVSS v3.1 7.5, CWE-190/CWE-122) sits in src/runner/utils/image_processor.cpp. Signed 32-bit stride multiplication in resize_pillow() and create_patches() wraps on image widths above 536,870,911 pixels. A negative wraparound cast to size_t requests petabyte allocations and throws std::bad_alloc; a positive wraparound allocates a tiny heap buffer that the pixel copy loop immediately overflows. Any network-exposed multimodal endpoint accepting image input is reachable here via T1190. CAN-2026-2038779 (CVSS v3.1 6.2, CWE-415) in src/cmdline.hpp is a Rule-of-Three double-free in the CLI parser: the class frees raw option_base heap pointers in its destructor without defining a copy constructor, so shallow copies corrupt glibc tcache freelists.  DFIR takeaway: The immediate hunt is firmware provenance. Pull the commit hash of the ax-llm BSP integrated into your edge appliances and compare against the four remediation commits (5ad6f17, 47405d2, 23faad8, 5dce054). If deployed firmware predates those commits, treat the device as compromised-capable and prioritize isolation, particularly any unit running multimodal audio or image ingestion. On a device you can inspect, look for /dev/ax_npu driver fault messages and garbled token output in inference logs as the observable indicator of the DMA corruption chain. The report's CWE and ATT&CK mappings (T1190, T1195.002, T1068, T1499.001) are in the Cobalt advisory for detection engineering alignment. Formal CVE records publish October 31, 2026.  #DFIR_Radar

オーストラリア信号局（ASD）が、「Essential-Eight」を発展させ、業務機能や資産のまとまりごとに対策の有効性を評価する「ASD-Essentials」を公表しています。成熟度レベルに代わり、リスクの低減効果を踏まえて取り組む順序を示す「優先フェーズ」を導入。成熟度レベルの判定から、業務や資産ごとに対策が有効に機能しているかを確かめる評価への移行です。  【要点の整理】  ・対象環境は企業IT、OT、SaaSとPaaSのみで提供されるクラウドの3章。主な読者は政府機関、重要インフラの所有者・運営者、大規模組織  ・共通の構成は、達成すべき成果を示す「原則」、実施事項の「アクション」、リスクの似た業務機能・資産をまとめる「ドメイン」。必要に応じてアクションとMITRE ATT&CKの攻撃手法を対応付け  ・企業ITの移行準備では、まず境界サービスとIDサービスを対象に、ガバナンス・文化、可視化・対応の能力も整備。優先フェーズは実施順序であり、成熟度の新しい点数ではないとの説明  ・各アクションをドメインごとに「有効でない」「部分的に有効」「完全に有効」で評価。従来の成熟度は自動換算せず、既存の対策・証拠を再利用して不足分を確認。AIも対象資産に含め、経営層の説明責任を規定  ・移行期間中は両枠組みを維持。進行中の対策強化は継続し、規制当局が変更を示すまでは現行の規制上の義務に対応  詳細は以下を参照： cyber.gov.au/news/asd-essent… cyber.gov.au/publication/fre…  (※可能な範囲でファクトチェックは実施済なものの、元記事の精度依存や速報・要約の性質上漏れもありうるため、正確な情報は一次情報を直接参照のこと)

Tarea 9 Elegir el marco adecuado Descripción general Ahora ya tienes conocimientos prácticos sobre varios marcos de trabajo para pruebas de penetración, cada uno con su propia filosofía, estructura y fortalezas. Sin embargo, saber qué es cada marco no te indica automáticamente cuál usar . En la práctica, la selección del marco de trabajo es una de las primeras decisiones que toma un especialista en pruebas de penetración tras recibir el briefing del proyecto, y es una decisión influenciada por múltiples factores que a menudo apuntan en direcciones opuestas.  Consideremos la analogía de la caja de herramientas de un mecánico. Un mecánico no usa todas las herramientas en cada trabajo; las selecciona según el vehículo, el problema y las expectativas del cliente. Un especialista en pruebas de penetración opera de la misma manera. El marco de trabajo adecuado depende del sector del cliente, el tipo de sistemas que se prueban, el marco regulatorio y los objetivos del proyecto.  Esta tarea repasa los criterios clave de selección y luego presenta escenarios realistas para que practiques la toma de decisiones.  Criterios de selección En proyectos reales, la selección del marco de trabajo depende sistemáticamente de cuatro factores.  El alcance del compromiso y el tipo de objetivo es el filtro más inmediato. Una evaluación de la aplicación web se alinea con el OWASP WSTG. La interacción mediante una aplicación móvil requiere OWASP MASTG. Una prueba de penetración de red de espectro completo se alinea naturalmente con PTES u OSSTMM. Si el alcance abarca múltiples canales, incluidos factores físicos y humanos, el modelo de cinco canales de OSSTMM resulta particularmente relevante.  Los requisitos normativos y de cumplimiento pueden anular por completo las preferencias personales. Si el cliente procesa datos de tarjetas de pago, PCI DSS Las directrices para las pruebas de penetración no son opcionales. Si el cliente es una institución financiera del Reino Unido sujeta a la supervisión del Banco de Inglaterra, es posible que se requiera la certificación CBEST. NIST La norma SP 800-115 tiene gran relevancia en el gobierno estadounidense y en el ámbito de los contratistas federales. Cuando la normativa lo exige, el técnico se adapta.  La necesidad de obtener resultados cuantificables y repetibles es fundamental cuando intervienen varios evaluadores o cuando es necesario comparar resultados a lo largo del tiempo. Las métricas RAV de OSSTMM están diseñadas específicamente para esto. Si un cliente afirma: «Queremos medir si nuestra postura de seguridad ha mejorado desde la prueba del año pasado», OSSTMM proporciona el marco de medición para responder objetivamente a esa pregunta.  La experiencia del equipo y los recursos disponibles son limitaciones prácticas que a menudo se pasan por alto. Una implementación completa de OSSTMM requiere un conocimiento profundo de su sistema de métricas. CBEST exige capacidades de inteligencia sobre amenazas. Para un equipo pequeño que realiza una evaluación estándar de la red corporativa, PTES ofrece un flujo de trabajo práctico y bien estructurado, sin la complejidad de marcos más especializados.  Práctica de escenarios Apliquemos estos criterios a situaciones realistas. Para cada escenario, considere qué marco (o combinación) recomendaría y por qué.  Escenario 1: Un hospital regional contrata a su equipo para probar su portal web para pacientes y la red interna a la que se conecta. El hospital debe cumplir con HIPAA pero no está sujeto a PCI DSS(Subcontrata el procesamiento de pagos). Quieren una evaluación estructurada e integral con un resumen ejecutivo claro para el consejo de administración.  PTES es la opción más adecuada en este caso. Proporciona la estructura de colaboración integral que el hospital necesita, su fase de informes genera explícitamente entregables tanto ejecutivos como técnicos, y abarca las pruebas de aplicaciones web y de red dentro de una única metodología. OWASP WSTG puede complementar las pruebas del portal web específicamente y mapear los hallazgos de MITRE ATT&CK Identificaciones El informe se vería reforzado al basarse en comportamientos de amenazas del mundo real.  Escenario 2: Un banco multinacional con sede en Londres necesita una prueba de penetración que cumpla con sus obligaciones regulatorias en el Reino Unido. El proceso debe comenzar con una evaluación de inteligencia de amenazas específica para la institución.  CBEST es la opción ideal. Está diseñado para instituciones financieras del Reino Unido, exige una fase específica de inteligencia sobre amenazas y está reconocido por el Banco de Inglaterra. Ningún marco de trabajo de propósito general por sí solo satisfaría estos requisitos.  Escenario 3: A SaaS La startup busca que dos empresas de seguridad diferentes prueben su plataforma de forma independiente durante los próximos dos años y comparen directamente los resultados para evaluar las mejoras. La plataforma es completamente web.  Las métricas RAV de OSSTMM permiten realizar comparaciones directas entre equipos y en diferentes momentos, tal como lo solicita el cliente. OWASP WSTG guiaría los casos de prueba específicos para la web, mientras que OSSTMM proporciona la capa de medición cuantitativa que hace que la comparación interanual sea significativa.  Escenario 4: Una empresa de tecnología financiera te pide que pruebes sus aplicaciones de banca móvil para Android e iOS, ambas destinadas a gestionar transacciones con tarjeta de crédito.  Este compromiso requiere que dos marcos de trabajo trabajen conjuntamente. OWASP MASTG proporciona los casos de prueba para la seguridad de las aplicaciones móviles en ambas plataformas. PCI DSS También deben seguirse las directrices de pruebas de penetración, ya que las aplicaciones manejan datos de titulares de tarjetas. El evaluador debe cumplir simultáneamente con la metodología de pruebas específica para dispositivos móviles y con la normativa vigente.  Notas finales Como ilustran estos escenarios, la selección de un marco de trabajo rara vez es una decisión única. Los proyectos reales suelen implicar un marco principal que estructura la metodología general y marcos complementarios que abordan requisitos regulatorios, de plataforma o de informes específicos. La capacidad de reconocer qué marcos de trabajo son aplicables y cómo se complementan entre sí es una habilidad que distingue a un probador de penetración metódico de alguien que simplemente utiliza herramientas.  Responda las siguientes preguntas Una agencia federal estadounidense necesita una evaluación de seguridad de su red interna. Los resultados deben ajustarse a las directrices federales, y la evaluación debe incluir tanto la revisión de documentos como pruebas de penetración activas. ¿Qué marco de trabajo es la opción principal más lógica?  NIST SP 800-115  Su cliente es una empresa de comercio electrónico con una tienda online, una aplicación móvil de compras y un sistema de procesamiento de pagos. ¿Qué combinación de frameworks recomendaría para cubrir los tres componentes? (separados por comas)  WSTG,MASTG,PCI DSS

Tarea 8 Otros marcos de trabajo destacables Descripción general Los marcos que hemos cubierto hasta ahora, OSSTMM,OWASPWSTG,NISTSP 800-115, PTES, ISSAF y MITRE ATT&CK representan las metodologías y bases de conocimiento fundamentales con las que probablemente se encontrará un probador de penetración junior. Pero el panorama no termina ahí. Dependiendo del sector, la plataforma o el entorno normativo en el que opere su cliente, es posible que deba conocer marcos de trabajo más especializados que aborden dominios específicos.  Esta tarea analiza cinco marcos de trabajo adicionales. El objetivo no es dominarlos a fondo, sino comprender su contexto : saber que existen, entender su función específica y reconocer cuándo un proyecto con un cliente podría requerir alguno de ellos.  Los marcos Clasificación de amenazas de WASC Fue desarrollada por el Consorcio de Seguridad de Aplicaciones Web (WASC) como una taxonomía para categorizar las vulnerabilidades y los tipos de ataques a aplicaciones web. Organiza las amenazas en categorías como autenticación insuficiente, fuga de información y abuso de funcionalidad. Si bien fue influyente a mediados de la década de 2000 y ayudó a estandarizar la forma en que la industria discutía las amenazas web, desde entonces ha sido reemplazada en gran medida por la OWASP Top Ten y WSTG son las principales referencias en seguridad web. Es posible que aún se mencionen en documentación antigua o marcos de cumplimiento normativo.  Matriz de Controles en la Nube (CCM) de CSA es publicado por la Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) y proporciona un marco de controles de ciberseguridad diseñado específicamente para entornos de computación en la nube . Mapea los controles en 17 dominios, incluyendo seguridad de datos, gestión de identidad y acceso, y seguridad de infraestructura, y los alinea con estándares importantes como ISO 27001,NIST, y PCI DSSCCM no es una metodología de pruebas de penetración; es una herramienta de gobernanza y cumplimiento que ayuda a las organizaciones a evaluar si sus proveedores y configuraciones en la nube cumplen con los requisitos de seguridad. Se utiliza cuando un cliente necesita una evaluación de la postura de seguridad en la nube en lugar de una prueba de penetración tradicional.  OWASP Guía de pruebas de seguridad para aplicaciones móviles (MASTG) es la contraparte móvil del WSTG que cubrimos en la Tarea 3. Mantenido por OWASP, el MASTG Proporciona casos de prueba detallados para la seguridad de aplicaciones Android e iOS , que cubren áreas como almacenamiento de datos, implementación criptográfica, comunicación de red, interacción de plataforma y calidad del código. Si su proyecto implica probar una aplicación de banca móvil, una aplicación de portal de pacientes de atención médica o cualquier aplicación móvil orientada al cliente, MASTG es la referencia ideal. Se utiliza junto con OWASP El Estándar de Verificación de Seguridad de Aplicaciones Móviles (MASVS , por sus siglas en inglés) define los requisitos de seguridad que el MASTG evalúa.  PCI DSS Directrices para las pruebas de penetración están definidos dentro del Estándar de Seguridad de Datos de la Industria de Tarjetas de Pago , específicamente en el Requisito 11.4 (PCI DSSv4.0). A diferencia de los marcos de propósito general cubiertos anteriormente, estas directrices son mandatos regulatorios : cualquier organización que procese, almacene o transmita datos de titulares de tarjetas debe realizar pruebas de penetración que cumplan PCI DSS criterios. Las directrices especifican que las pruebas deben cubrir tanto el perímetro externo como la red interna, deben realizarse al menos anualmente y después de cambios significativos en la infraestructura, y deben validar la red. Segmentación controles. Cuando su cliente es un minorista, un procesador de pagos o cualquier entidad en el ecosistema de tarjetas de pago, PCI DSS Los requisitos determinarán tanto el alcance como el formato de los informes de su proyecto.  Marco CBEST CBEST fue desarrollado por el Banco de Inglaterra en colaboración con el sector financiero del Reino Unido. Se trata de un marco de pruebas de penetración basado en inteligencia de amenazas, diseñado específicamente para instituciones financieras británicas , incluyendo bancos, aseguradoras y proveedores de infraestructura del mercado financiero. Los proyectos CBEST comienzan con una fase personalizada de inteligencia de amenazas que identifica a los actores de amenazas y escenarios de ataque más relevantes para la institución en cuestión. La posterior prueba de penetración simula esos escenarios de amenazas realistas. CBEST destaca por su estrecha integración de la inteligencia de amenazas con pruebas prácticas y por su respaldo regulatorio dentro del sector financiero del Reino Unido.  Notas finales La conclusión principal de esta encuesta es que la selección del marco está determinada por el contexto . La industria del cliente, las obligaciones regulatorias, la plataforma tecnológica y la jurisdicción geográfica influyen en qué marco se aplica. Un probador de penetración que trabaja con un banco del Reino Unido debe comprender CBEST. Un probador que evalúa una aplicación de salud móvil recurrirá aOWASPMASTG. Un probador que trabaja con un procesador de pagos no puede evitarPCI DSSRequisitos. Conocer el panorama significa que puedes reconocer qué marco de trabajo exige un proyecto determinado, incluso si necesitas estudiarlo en detalle en ese momento.  Responda las siguientes preguntas Su cliente es un minorista europeo en línea que procesa pagos con tarjeta de crédito a través de su sitio web. ¿Qué marco de trabajo de esta tarea regiría más directamente los requisitos de las pruebas de penetración para este proyecto?  PCI DSS Penetration Testing Guidelines  Un cliente te pide que evalúes la seguridad de su aplicación bancaria para iOS, incluyendo cómo almacena las credenciales localmente y se comunica con las API de backend. ¿Qué framework de esta tarea es la referencia de prueba más apropiada?  OWASP Mobile Application Security Testing Guide  Tu equipo está evaluando la infraestructura de AWS de un cliente para determinar si sus configuraciones en la nube cumplen con los estándares de seguridad del sector. No solicitan una prueba de penetración, sino una evaluación de controles. ¿Qué marco de trabajo es el más adecuado?  CSA Cloud Control Matrix

Tarea 7 MITRE ATT&CK  En las tareas anteriores, exploramos marcos que le indican cómo realizar una prueba de penetración: cómo definir su alcance, avanzar por las fases e informar sobre sus hallazgos. Pero considere esta situación: acaba de completar un proyecto utilizando PTES, y el informe documenta que obtuvo acceso inicial a través de un Correo electrónico de phishing, privilegios elevados mediante la explotación de un servicio mal configurado, movimiento lateral con credenciales robadas y filtración de datos a través de un canal cifrado. Su cliente lee el informe y formula una pregunta aparentemente sencilla: «¿Cómo se compara nuestra exposición con las acciones reales de los ciberdelincuentes?».  Esa pregunta es difícil de responder solo con un marco de pruebas de penetración. Marcos como PTES y OSSTMM estructuran su proceso de pruebas, pero no catalogan sistemáticamente las tácticas y técnicas específicas que utilizan los adversarios del mundo real. Esta es la brecha que MITRE ATT&CK rellena.  ATT&CK significa Tácticas, Técnicas y Conocimientos Comunes Adversarios . Desarrollado y mantenido por Mitre Corporación No se trata de un marco de pruebas de penetración tradicional. Es una base de conocimientos sobre el comportamiento de los adversarios, construida a partir de observaciones reales de cómo operan los ciberdelincuentes. Cataloga las acciones de los atacantes, organizadas en una estructura que los profesionales de la seguridad pueden utilizar para la inteligencia de amenazas, la ingeniería de detección, las pruebas de penetración (red teaming) y, en lo que respecta a esta sala, para enriquecer los resultados de las pruebas de penetración.  Matrix: tácticas, técnicas y subtécnicas ATT&CK está organizado como una matriz . Piénselo como una tabla grande. Las columnas representan tácticas , que son los objetivos de alto nivel del adversario, el porqué de una acción. La matriz Enterprise actual incluye 14 tácticas, que progresan desde el acceso inicial hasta la ejecución ,persistencia escalada de privilegios, evasión de defensas, acceso a credenciales, descubrimiento, movimiento lateral, recopilación, comando y control, exfiltración e impacto.  Dentro de cada columna de táctica, las filas enumeran las técnicas , que son el cómo , los métodos específicos que un adversario utiliza para lograr ese objetivo táctico. Por ejemplo, bajo la táctica Acceso Inicial, encontrará técnicas como Suplantación de identidad ( T1566), Explotar aplicaciones de cara al público ( T1190) y cuentas válidas ( T1078). Muchas técnicas se dividen a su vez en subtécnicas . El phishing, por ejemplo, tiene subtécnicas para archivos adjuntos de spearphishing ( T1566.001), enlaces de spearphishing ( T1566.002) y spearphishing a través de servicios ( T1566.003).  Cada técnica de la base de conocimientos ATT&CK incluye una descripción, ejemplos reales de grupos de amenazas que la han utilizado, recomendaciones de detección y medidas de mitigación. Esto convierte a ATT&CK en algo más que una taxonomía; es una referencia dinámica vinculada al comportamiento observado de los adversarios.  ATT&CK como complemento, no como reemplazo. Aquí radica la clave para esta distinción: ATT&CK no indica cómo realizar una prueba de penetración. No define fases, procedimientos de alcance ni formatos de informe. En cambio, proporciona un lenguaje común para describir los hallazgos de una prueba realizada con cualquier marco de trabajo.  Consideremos la analogía entre un diccionario médico y un procedimiento diagnóstico. El PTES es como el procedimiento diagnóstico: le indica al médico los pasos a seguir durante un examen. El ATT&CK es como el diccionario médico: proporciona terminología estandarizada para nombrar y categorizar lo que el médico observa. Ambos son necesarios, pero cumplen funciones diferentes.  Mediante la anotación de un informe PTES con la técnica ATT&CK. El evaluador proporciona al equipo de seguridad de MedGuard información práctica que va más allá de la simple corrección de vulnerabilidades individuales. El cliente ahora puede consultar cada técnica en la base de conocimientos de ATT&CK, revisar la guía de detección y crear o validar reglas de detección para esos comportamientos específicos. La conversación pasa de «corregir este error» a «¿podemos detectar este tipo de comportamiento del adversario?».  Notas finales La fortaleza de ATT&CK reside en su función como traductor universal del comportamiento de los adversarios. Permite que los pentesters, analistas de inteligencia de amenazas, ingenieros de detección y equipos de respuesta a incidentes hablen el mismo idioma. Para los pentesters en particular, mapear los hallazgos a ATT&CK transforma un informe, pasando de ser una simple lista de vulnerabilidades a una narrativa basada en el comportamiento real de las amenazas.  La base de conocimientos es extensa y dominarla requiere tiempo. La matriz Enterprise, por sí sola, contiene más de 200 técnicas. Para una exploración más profunda y práctica de ATT&CK, incluyendo cómo navegar por la matriz, investigar grupos de amenazas específicos y aplicarla a la ingeniería de detección, las salas dedicadas más adelante en la plataforma TryHackMe cubren ATT&CK con mucho más detalle. Por ahora, la conclusión esencial es esta: ATT&CK complementa el marco de pruebas de penetración que elijas al proporcionar un vocabulario estandarizado para lo que encuentres.  Responda las siguientes preguntas En la matriz ATT&CK, ¿qué representan las columnas?  tactics  En la matriz ATT&CK, ¿qué representan las filas dentro de cada columna?  techniques  Usted comprometió un servidor web al explotar una vulnerabilidad sin parchear en su aplicación de cara al público. ¿Qué identificador de técnica de ATT&CK utilizaría para clasificar este hallazgo?  T1190

The Gospel writers leave small details that fit together when you compare their accounts, corroborating each other as sources. That is the argument from “undesigned coincidences.”  Here is a catalog drawn from the youtube channel Testify (Eric Manning).   INTERLOCKING GOSPEL DETAILS  1. Mark’s two-by-two mission fits Matthew’s paired apostle list. Matthew presents the Twelve in pairs: Peter and Andrew, James and John, and so on. Mark’s list has a different arrangement, but his mission account says Jesus sent them out two by two. That gives a practical reason for Matthew’s grouping. Scripture: Matthew 10:1–4; Mark 3:16–19; 6:7.  2. Joanna offers a plausible channel for news of Herod’s private remarks. Matthew reports Herod telling his servants that Jesus must be John the Baptist raised from the dead. Luke names Joanna, wife of Chuza, Herod’s household manager, among Jesus’ supporters. This puts someone with a palace connection in Jesus’ circle: a plausible channel for such news. Scripture: Matthew 14:1–2; Luke 8:1–3.  3. James and John’s fiery response fits their “Sons of Thunder” nickname. Mark gives James and John the nickname “Sons of Thunder,” without explanation. Luke omits the name but describes those brothers wanting to call fire from heaven on a Samaritan village that refused Jesus. Their forceful response suits the nickname. Scripture: Mark 3:17; Luke 9:51–55.  4. Earlier Jerusalem confrontations could explain scrutiny from the capital. Mark describes scribes and Pharisees coming from Jerusalem to scrutinize Jesus in Galilee. John narrates earlier Jerusalem confrontations over the temple and a Sabbath healing, including opponents seeking Jesus’ death. Scripture: Mark 3:22; 7:1; John 2:13–22; 5:1–18.  5. John’s repeated Jerusalem visits fit Jesus’ lament about his repeated appeals. Jesus laments how often he wanted to gather Jerusalem’s children, but they were unwilling. The Synoptics concentrate on his Galilean ministry and final approach to Jerusalem; John describes several earlier festival visits. Scripture: Matthew 23:37; Luke 13:34; John 2:13; 5:1; 7:10; 10:22–23.  6. Philip’s Bethsaida roots fit Jesus’ choice to ask him about buying bread. John records Jesus asking Philip where to buy bread for the crowd, and elsewhere identifies Philip as being from Bethsaida. Luke places the feeding near that town. A local man would be a natural person to ask about supplies. Scripture: John 6:5–7; 1:44; 12:21; Luke 9:10–17.  7. Andrew’s Bethsaida roots fit his involvement with the boy and his food. Andrew identifies the boy with five loaves and two fish. John says Andrew, like Philip, came from Bethsaida; Luke places the feeding near Bethsaida. Both men’s involvement thus fits the location. Scripture: John 1:44; 6:8–9; Luke 9:10.  8. The approaching Passover offers a background for the crowds coming and going. Mark says people were coming and going so constantly that Jesus and the disciples had no leisure even to eat, prompting their withdrawal by boat. John places the feeding near Passover, a time of travel to Jerusalem. Festival traffic could help explain the bustle. Scripture: Mark 6:30–31; John 6:4.  9. The spring Passover setting fits Mark’s green grass. Mark describes the crowd sitting on green grass; John says there was much grass and Passover was near. Passover falls in spring after the winter rains, when green vegetation is natural in Galilee. Scripture: Mark 6:39; John 6:4, 10.  10. The barley loaves fit the Passover harvest season. John specifies barley loaves. Barley’s spring harvest fits Passover and Mark’s green grass. Leviticus places the firstfruits offering in the festival period. Scripture: John 6:4, 9, 13; Mark 6:39; compare Leviticus 23:5–14.  11. Organized seating makes the count of about 5,000 men understandable. Mark describes groups of hundreds and fifties; Luke records groups of about fifty. Organized seating makes distribution and an approximate count easier. Matthew distinguishes the roughly 5,000 men from women and children; John also specifies men when giving the number. Scripture: Matthew 14:21; Mark 6:39–44; Luke 9:14–15; John 6:10.  12. Luke supplies examples of ministry that fit the rebuke of Bethsaida. Matthew rebukes Bethsaida for not repenting despite mighty works, but does not locate his feeding account there. Luke places the feeding near Bethsaida and also describes healings before it. Scripture: Matthew 11:20–21; 14:13–21; Luke 9:10–17; 10:13.  13. Bethsaida’s rebuke offers a possible interpretation of the healing outside the village. Mark says Jesus took the blind man outside Bethsaida to heal him, then told him not to enter the village. Matthew and Luke preserve a judgment against Bethsaida’s unrepentance. Manning proposes this as a reason for keeping the healing outside. Scripture: Mark 8:22–26; Matthew 11:21; Luke 10:13.  14. John’s Capernaum account illustrates the rejection reflected in Matthew’s woe. Matthew warns Capernaum despite its mighty works. John places the bread discourse there and describes misunderstanding, objections, and many disciples abandoning Jesus. This illustrates rejection amid remarkable ministry. Scripture: Matthew 11:23–24; John 6:24–26, 59–66.  15. The attempted kingship supplies a reason for caution about publicity. Mark repeatedly shows Jesus restricting publicity or disclosure of his identity. John supplies a concrete danger: after the feeding, the crowd wants to seize Jesus and make him king, so he withdraws. Such enthusiasm could turn his mission into a political movement. It offers one reason for caution. Scripture: Mark 1:43–45; 8:29–30; John 6:14–15.  16. The Jerusalem healing could have contributed to Bartimaeus’ confidence. Bartimaeus persistently asks Jesus to restore his sight near Jericho. John describes a much-discussed healing of a man born blind in Jerusalem, with people still referring to it afterward. News of that event could have reached and encouraged Bartimaeus. Scripture: Mark 10:46–52; John 9:1–7; 11:37.  17. Matthew’s explicit application reinforces Luke’s vineyard warning. In Jesus’ vineyard parable, Luke has the owner destroy the tenants and give the vineyard to others, prompting “May it never be!” Matthew applies it explicitly: the kingdom will be taken from the hearers and given to a people producing its fruit. Matthew clarifies the warning’s meaning. Scripture: Luke 20:9–19; Matthew 21:33–45, especially 21:43.  18. John’s dates and Mark’s sequence permit a matching Passion Week countdown. John dates Jesus’ arrival at Bethany six days before Passover and the entry to the next day. Mark traces days through the entry, fig tree, temple activity, and teaching, then says Passover is two days away. Scripture: John 12:1–2, 12–15; Mark 11:1–20, 27; 13:1–3; 14:1.  19. Luke’s supper dispute fits John’s foot-washing lesson. Luke describes a supper dispute about which disciple was greatest, followed by Jesus’ teaching about serving. John describes Jesus taking a towel, washing their feet, and telling them to serve one another, without mentioning the quarrel. The dispute supplies a fitting occasion for the acted lesson. Scripture: Luke 22:24–27; John 13:3–17.  20. John’s foot washing illustrates Luke’s saying about serving. At supper in Luke, Jesus says he is among the disciples as one who serves, without describing a particular act at that meal. John has him rise from supper, wash their feet, and explain the example. The act vividly illustrates Luke’s saying. Scripture: Luke 22:27; John 13:4–5, 12–16.  21. The bread and cup sayings complement John’s flesh-and-blood discourse. John has Jesus speak of giving his flesh for the world’s life and of eating his flesh and drinking his blood. John omits the bread-and-cup institution at the Last Supper, which the Synoptics record. Both sayings concern Jesus’ self-giving. Scripture: John 6:51–58; Matthew 26:26–28; Mark 14:22–24; Luke 22:19–20.  22. The Gethsemane prayer illuminates John’s reference to the Father’s cup. At the arrest, John has Jesus tell Peter to put away his sword and accept the cup the Father has given him. John omits the Gethsemane prayer about that cup, which the Synoptics preserve. Their prayer scene supplies immediate background for John’s saying. The cup is also a suffering image elsewhere. Scripture: John 18:10–11; Mark 14:35–36; Matthew 26:39; Luke 22:42; compare Mark 10:38–39.  23. John preserves the original saying behind the Synoptic temple-destruction accusation. Mark’s trial witnesses and mockers accuse Jesus of promising to destroy and rebuild the temple. John supplies “Destroy this temple” and “in three days I will raise it up,” explaining that Jesus meant his body. John omits the trial accusation. His saying fits the distorted report: a challenge about his body becomes a threat against the building. The Synoptics also predict the temple’s destruction elsewhere. Scripture: Mark 14:57–59; 15:29–30; Matthew 26:60–61; John 2:18–22; compare Mark 13:1–2.  24. The blindfold explains the demand to prophesy who struck Jesus. Matthew’s mockers strike Jesus and demand that he prophesy who hit him, without mentioning a blindfold. Luke supplies it: they blindfold him before demanding the assailant’s identity. This explains why identifying the attacker would require supernatural knowledge. Mark also mentions covering his face. Scripture: Matthew 26:67–68; Luke 22:63–65; compare Mark 14:65.  25. Luke’s political charge explains Pilate’s kingship question in John. John moves from the accusers’ general claim that Jesus is an evildoer to Pilate’s specific question about being king of the Jews. Luke supplies the political charge: misleading the nation, opposing tribute, and claiming to be Christ, a king. Luke’s fuller accusation explains the subject of John’s interrogation; each preserves different parts of the exchange. Scripture: John 18:29–33; Luke 23:1–3.  26. John’s fuller reply helps explain Pilate’s verdict in Luke. Luke gives a brief kingship exchange and Pilate’s finding of no guilt. John supplies a longer reply: Jesus’ kingdom is not from this world, and his servants are not fighting to prevent his arrest. Pilate then declares no fault. That reply helps explain why Pilate could distinguish Jesus’ kingship from the armed revolt implied by the accusation. Scripture: Luke 23:2–4; John 18:33–38.  27. Luke’s healing adds to John’s account of Jesus stopping Peter’s violence. John names Peter as the disciple who cuts off the servant’s ear and records Jesus ordering him to put away the sword. Luke adds that Jesus healed the injury, repairing the harm his disciple caused. That detail further illustrates Jesus’ rejection of the violence and fits his later statement in John that his servants were not fighting to prevent his arrest. Scripture: John 18:10–11, 36; Luke 22:49–51.  28. The high-priest connection could explain John’s household knowledge. John names the injured servant Malchus and identifies a courtyard questioner as his relative. He also says another disciple was known to the high priest and secured courtyard access. That household connection offers a plausible channel for knowing its people.  Scripture: John 18:10, 15–16, 26.  29. John’s account of Joseph’s fear explains the courage emphasized by Mark. Mark says Joseph took courage to ask Pilate for Jesus’ body. John says he had kept his discipleship secret because he feared the Jewish authorities. Publicly requesting the executed Jesus’ body exposed an allegiance previously concealed. That background makes Mark’s emphasis on courage especially fitting, though other risks could also have mattered. Scripture: Mark 15:43; John 19:38–39.  30. Joseph’s tomb ownership explains the burial place’s availability. John describes a nearby, unused garden tomb, chosen with the burial deadline approaching. Luke also says no one had been laid there. Matthew adds that the wealthy Joseph owned this newly cut tomb. His ownership explains his ready access to it, while “new” fits its unused condition. The accounts supply different practical details of the same burial. Scripture: John 19:41–42; Luke 23:53; Matthew 27:57–60.  31. Herod’s rule in Perea makes a threat beyond Galilee plausible. Luke records a warning that Herod wants Jesus killed on his journey toward Jerusalem, without naming Perea. Other Gospels place late ministry beyond the Jordan; Josephus says Antipas ruled Perea as well as Galilee. Leaving Galilee therefore need not mean leaving Herod’s jurisdiction.  Scripture: Luke 13:22, 31–33; Matthew 19:1; Mark 10:1; John 10:40. Background: Josephus, Antiquities 17.8.1.  RELATED GOSPEL CORRESPONDENCES  32. John’s soldiers complement Mark’s official confirmation of death. Mark says Pilate was surprised Jesus had died so soon and checked with the centurion before releasing the body. John describes soldiers finding Jesus dead, leaving his legs unbroken, and piercing his side. Scripture: Mark 15:39, 44–45; John 19:31–35.  33. Mary Magdalene’s plural “we” fits the other Gospels’ companions. John introduces Mary Magdalene going to the tomb, then has her report, “we do not know” where Jesus has been laid. The other Gospels name women visiting together. The plural fits John focusing on one member of a group rather than asserting she was alone. Scripture: John 20:1–2; Matthew 28:1; Mark 16:1; Luke 24:1, 10.  34. Peter’s immediate entry into the tomb fits his impulsive behavior elsewhere. John’s other disciple reaches the tomb first but waits outside; Peter arrives and goes straight in. Matthew has Peter volunteer to step onto the water toward Jesus; John later has him plunge into the sea to reach Jesus. Peter’s readiness to act is recorded across three very different scenes. Scripture: John 20:3–6; Matthew 14:28–31; compare John 21:7.  35. Peter’s boast offers a background for Jesus’ question about his love. Mark and Matthew record Peter boasting that he will remain faithful even if everyone else falls away. John has the risen Jesus ask whether Peter loves him “more than these.” If this means more than the other disciples love Jesus, it recalls Peter’s comparison.  Scripture: John 21:15–17; Mark 14:29–31; Matthew 26:33–35.  36. Mary and Martha retain consistent personalities across different stories. Luke shows Martha busy serving while Mary sits at Jesus’ feet. John has Martha go out to meet Jesus, raise a practical concern at Lazarus’ tomb, and later serve; Mary stays seated until called, falls at Jesus’ feet, and later anoints them. Their recurring differences fit distinct scenes. Martha also voices strong faith, so neither sister need be reduced to stereotype. Scripture: Luke 10:38–42; John 11:20, 28–33, 39; 12:1–3.  37. Joseph’s repeated absence fits the inference that he had died. Joseph appears in Jesus’ childhood but is absent from later scenes naming Mary and Jesus’ siblings. At the cross, Jesus entrusts Mary to the beloved disciple; Acts later names her with the brothers. Joseph’s death would explain both the repeated absence and the provision for Mary. Scripture: Luke 2:41–52; Mark 3:31–35; 6:3; John 2:12; 19:26–27; Acts 1:14.  38. Paul’s Rufus could explain Mark’s reference to Simon’s family. Mark calls Simon the father of Alexander and Rufus, without introducing the sons. Paul greets a Rufus and his mother in his letter to Rome. If this is the same man, Mark’s identification makes sense for readers acquainted with the family. Scripture: Mark 15:21; Romans 16:13.  39. Consistent basket vocabulary distinguishes the two feeding accounts. The Greek accounts of the 5,000 use kophinos for the twelve leftover baskets; those of the 4,000 use spyris for the seven. Matthew and Mark retain both terms when Jesus recalls the events. Acts uses spyris for the basket that lowered Paul through the wall. The distinction survives across the tellings but can disappear in English, where both words may simply be rendered “basket.” Scripture: Matthew 14:20; 15:37; 16:9–10; Mark 6:43; 8:8, 19–20; Luke 9:17; John 6:13; Acts 9:25.  RELATED EXTERNAL COINCIDENCES  40. Temple and regnal dates offer a chronological comparison. John records forty-six years of temple construction. Josephus dates Herod’s rebuilding initiative to his eighteenth regnal year; Luke dates John the Baptist’s ministry to Tiberius’ fifteenth. Comparing the markers can place the opening ministry in the late 20s AD on common reckonings. Exact synchronization depends on how the regnal years and construction interval are counted. Scripture: John 2:19–20; Luke 3:1–3, 21–23. Background: Josephus, Antiquities 15.11.1.  41. Herod’s marriage links the Gospel account with Josephus’ war narrative. The Gospels say John criticized Herod’s marriage. Josephus connects that marriage dispute with the war against Aretas and reports that some Jews saw Herod’s defeat as punishment for killing John. The scandal, execution, and public interpretation fit a shared setting.  Scripture: Matthew 14:3–4; Mark 6:17–20; Luke 3:19–20. Background: Josephus, Antiquities 18.5.1–2.  42. Samaritan hostility fits the refusal of Jerusalem-bound travelers. Luke says a Samaritan village refused Jesus because he was heading to Jerusalem. Josephus describes a later attack on Galileans taking the Samaritan route to a Jerusalem festival. That parallels hostility tied to this route and destination. It supplies historical background for Luke’s scene. Scripture: Luke 9:51–53; John 4:20. Background: Josephus, Antiquities 20.6.1.  43. The covered portico fits John’s winter setting. John explicitly notes winter at the Feast of Dedication and places Jesus walking in Solomon’s portico. A covered colonnade offers a plausible sheltered setting for conversation then. Scripture: John 10:22–23.  44. The feast’s water ceremony fits the living-water invitation. John places Jesus’ invitation to the thirsty during Booths. The Mishnah describes festival water drawn from Siloam and poured at the temple, supplying a concrete background for living-water language. Scripture: John 7:2, 37–39. Background: Mishnah Sukkah 4:9.  45. The feast’s illumination fits Jesus’ light saying. John places the light-of-the-world saying in the temple treasury, in the narrative surrounding Booths. The Mishnah describes great lamps lighting the Court of the Women during the feast. This offers a possible visual background for Jesus’ words near the treasury. Scripture: John 8:12, 20; compare John 7:2. Background: Mishnah Sukkah 5:2–3.  46. Passover charity makes the disciples’ guess about Judas plausible. The disciples guess that Judas’ nighttime departure concerns festival supplies or gifts to the poor. John identifies him as the money keeper. The Mishnah requires Passover wine even for the poor, illustrating concern for needy celebrants. This makes their guess culturally plausible. Scripture: John 13:27–30; compare John 12:6. Background: Mishnah Pesachim 10:1.  47. The four garment shares fit Roman guard arrangements. John’s four shares, one per soldier, imply four men. Acts describes four squads of four guarding Peter: sixteen assigned overall, with four in each squad. That supplies a comparison for a four-man unit, not a universal rule for executions. John separately explains casting lots for the tunic: it was seamless and the soldiers chose not to tear it. Scripture: John 19:23–24; compare Acts 12:4.  48. Philo’s Pilate fits John’s threat of an appeal to Caesar. John’s accusers say releasing Jesus would show disloyalty to Caesar. Philo describes Pilate fearing an appeal exposing his abuses to Tiberius, who ordered him to remove controversial shields. This illustrates the political vulnerability that makes John’s threat credible. Scripture: John 19:12–16. Background: Philo, Embassy to Gaius 299–305.  49. Gerizim’s history fits the Samaritan woman’s ancestral appeal. The woman contrasts her ancestors’ mountain worship with Jewish insistence on Jerusalem. Josephus discusses the rival Gerizim sanctuary and its destruction under John Hyrcanus, supplying background for that dispute.  Scripture: John 4:20–24. Background: Josephus, Antiquities 13.3.4; 13.9.1.  50. Different expectations could explain Jesus’ openness in Samaria. The woman expects a Messiah who explains all things; Jesus identifies himself to her. John 6 instead shows a crowd trying to force kingship on him. Manning proposes that a Moses-like teaching-prophet expectation made disclosure less liable to political misunderstanding.  Scripture: John 4:25–26; 6:15; compare Deuteronomy 18:15–18.  The force of the argument is cumulative. These connections are offered as evidence that the writers knew the people and events they describe.

CHINESE SCAM ALERT   THE TOOL WAS BUILT FOR TESTING. THEN IT WALKED INTO KOREAN BANKS. Artex is the name that landed this month. It is not the only Chinese AI product in the series.  ARTEX is an open-source AI agent released in 2026 by a Chinese developer who posts as Autumn-27 (named in reporting as Li Puhua). It was built to automate penetration testing. It does not run its own model. It connects to outside ones, including Claude, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek. On 8 October 2026 the developer pulled it from public view and made it closed-source, citing misuse. The GitHub page came down the same day. CrowdStrike tied a campaign against South Korean banks to a likely China-based, Chinese-speaking, financially motivated operator, estimated around 26. The firm said the attacker used Artex together with Anthropic’s Claude Code. At least seven to nine financial institutions were hit or targeted between late September and early October. Roughly 68,000 people had personal data exposed, including names, phone numbers, incomes, and loan limits. Shinhan Bank took the largest share, around 25,000 records. South Korean authorities called Artex use “highly likely.” A Korean firm later pointed at possible prior activity in a Chinese DDoS-for-hire group called GodNet/Vitas. That is attribution and allegation. It is not a conviction. The other Chinese AI tools already in the scam economy Haotian is a Chinese-language face-swap platform that sold on Telegram and integrated with WhatsApp and WeChat. WIRED and researchers linked it to pig-butchering operators who used it for live video calls. Compounds have dedicated “AI rooms.” Leaked chats from one site show workers scheduling a single model for deepfake calls because one person can only run one at a time. OpenAI has banned clusters of accounts that appeared to originate in Cambodia and used models to translate and generate romance and investment scam text in Japanese, Chinese, and English. Workers in the compounds are trained on ChatGPT and DeepSeek to sound natural. Bloomberg mapped Xinbi vendors selling AI and deepfake software for a few hundred to a few thousand dollars. The photo rule from the Prince Group papers, “not too beautiful,” now has a real-time face behind it. The spying and hacking side, without the manual Chinese state-linked intrusion groups are a standing public record. So is North Korea’s Lazarus, which the FBI attributed to the $1.5 billion Bybit theft. What this series has already posted is the bridge: Chinese organized-crime desks, including the one ZachXBT walked into under the name Jimmy Green, that launder for those state units. Artex is the newer piece. An open tool built in China for defensive testing was used, according to CrowdStrike, against Korean banks by a financially motivated Chinese-speaking operator. Data on tens of thousands of people left the building. The developer shut the public version after the fact. The lesson for the series The girl on WhatsApp can now hold a video call with a face that is not hers. The chat can be drafted by a model trained on Chinese. The data behind a Korean bank account can leave through a tool whose author is Chinese and whose public code is now gone. None of that requires you to understand the code. If a stranger wants a video call before the investment pitch, or a site wants more of your documents after the first deposit, the face and the form are both products. Check the SFC list. Do not pay the second voice. #Artex #Autumn27 #KoreanBanks #Haotian #Deepfake #PigButchering #Claude #Xinbi #CryptoScam #ScamAlert

Think about this for a second.  What happens when an open-source model reaches Mythos 6 level capability at finding bugs and carrying out attacks end to end?  No guardrails. No refusals. You tell it what you want, and it figures out the rest.  Now imagine any script kiddie pointing that thing at real infrastructure.  Just like Mr. Robot  Elliot and fsociety take down E Corp, wipe out its debt records, and throw the global economy into chaos.  In the show, that took a genius and months of planning.  What if it only takes a few prompts?  Now think about Web3.  Bybit lost $1.5B in a single attack attributed to Lazarus hacking group.  What once required an entire operation could eventually be pulled off by one person.  And why stop at one protocol? Imagine bridges, lending markets, and oracles being targeted simultaneously.  The attacker wouldn't even need to understand Solidity. The model would do the heavy lifting.  As of "Adding guardrails."  That's the problem with open weights. Anyone can modify them. Search Hugging Face for "abliterated" and you'll find models with their refusal mechanisms stripped away.  And here's the bigger problem!  While offensive capabilities are getting cheaper and more accessible, the whole system is unfair toward SRs.  • Researchers are now being charged non-refundable fees just to submit vulnerabilities, even when they're duplicates of privately known issues. • Bounty rewards are getting slashed. • Some projects are abandoning bug bounty programs altogether.  Think about how absurd that is.  We're approaching a world where finding and exploiting vulnerabilities could become almost effortless, yet we're making it increasingly difficult to justify finding and reporting them responsibly.  Offense is getting cheaper by the month. Defense is getting defunded.  And when that model finally drops, who do you think have better motives?  Reporting or Exploiting?

Opening it installed Hookedge, giving the Russian-linked group months of access.  🔑 Key facts: ▪️ First confirmed infection: 24 July ▪️ Activity seen as late as 24 September ▪️ Initial access: spear-phishing attachment (T1566.001) ▪️ Undocumented tool decrypted and ran code in memory (T1055) ▪️ Credential theft, likely via dumping (T1003), then recon and lateral movement ▪️ No C2 details, IoCs or CVEs disclosed  ⚠️ Why it matters: Stolen credentials and network maps could expose design specs, procurement data and operational plans tied to NATO defense readiness.  🛡️ Do this now: 1⃣ Sandbox Office attachments, block macros by default 2⃣ Detect in-memory execution and anomalous PowerShell or scripting 3⃣ Enforce MFA, watch privileged accounts for atypical use 4⃣ Segment engineering and law-enforcement networks 5⃣ Hunt for the Hookedge binary name, related registry keys and scheduled tasks  🔗 badgersignal.com/articles/ap… #APT28 #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity #DefenseIndustry #BadgerSignal

[8] 날씨·생활 가을비와 기온 하락 (남부·제주 중심 가을비, 이후 찬 공기 유입으로 쌀쌀) 핵심내용: 20일 오후부터 전남·경남·제주를 중심으로 비가 내리고 충청·경기 남부 등에도 약한 비가 예상된다. 비가 그친 뒤 북쪽에서 찬 공기가 내려오면서 기온이 크게 떨어지고 바람이 강해 체감온도가 낮아지겠다. 서울 등 중부 아침 기온은 한 자릿수까지 내려갈 전망이다. 인사이트: 일교차가 큰 가을철 건강 관리와 야외 활동 주의가 필요하다. 주 후반 영하권 추위 가능성도 제기된다.  [9] 정책·정치·외교 국정감사 공방 (국감 2주차, 부동산·외교·사법 등 여야 전면전) 핵심내용: 국회 국정감사가 이어지며 서울 집값·주택 공급, 한미 외교, 공소청 출범 이후 첫 국감 등에서 여야 공방이 가열되고 있다. 추미애 경기도지사 관련 논란과 은행권 해킹 책임론도 쟁점으로 부상했다. 민생 현안보다 정치 쟁점이 부각된다는 지적도 나온다. 인사이트: 정책 신뢰 회복을 위한 실질적 민생 논의가 부족하다는 평가가 많다. 국감 후반부 정책 성과 검증이 주목된다. [11] 기술·AI AI 음악 저작권 (AI 음악 저작권 신청 급증…기준 미비로 논란) 핵심내용: AI를 활용한 음악의 저작권 신청이 1년 새 500% 가까이 급증했으나 명확한 기준이 없어 대부분 미등록 상태다. 음저협이 AI 보조 창작에 대한 등록 기준을 마련했다가 철회하는 등 혼란이 이어지고 있다. 차트에 오르는 AI 보조 곡도 등장했다. 인사이트: 창작 주체와 AI 기여도 구분 기준 마련이 시급하다. 문화 산업 전반의 저작권 제도 정비가 필요하다.  [12] 사회·기타 가상자산 과세 준비 (정부, 가상자산 과세 앞두고 5대 거래소 첫 소집) 핵심내용: 정부가 가상자산 과세를 앞두고 국내 5대 거래소를 처음으로 소집해 관련 사항을 점검했다. 과세 인프라와 정보 제공 체계 구축이 주요 논의 주제다. 시장에서는 과세 시점과 범위에 대한 관심이 높다. 인사이트: 가상자산 시장 제도화 속도가 빨라지고 있다. 투자자 보호와 세수 확보 사이의 균형이 과제다.  [13] 경제·증시·기업 현대차그룹 방산 일원화 (현대차그룹, 지상무기 사업 현대로템으로 통합) 핵심내용: 현대차그룹이 현대로템·현대위아 등에 흩어져 있던 지상무기 사업을 현대로템으로 일원화하기로 했다. 방산 사업의 시너지와 효율성 제고를 위한 조치다. K2 전차 등 수출 성과가 이어지는 가운데 조직 재편이 진행된다. 인사이트: 글로벌 방산 수요 증가 속에서 국내 기업의 경쟁력 강화 움직임이다. 중장기 수주 확대 가능성이 있다. 오늘의 뉴스분석 ☆  2026년 10월 19일 월요일  1. 삼전닉스 폭락에 3년치 국민연금, 3개월 만에 사라졌다 → 3개월 동안 평가액 182조 감소. 이는 국민연금이 거둬들이는 3년치 연금보험료에 해당. 올 초 규정을 바꿔가며 이익 실현 시기를 놓친 데 대해 또다시 질타 여론...(서울)  2. 한일 경제 역전 → 1980년 한국의 1인당 GDP는 일본의 17%에 불과했다. 지금 한국은 실질 구매력에서는 10년째, 명목소득에서는 3년째 일본을 앞서고 있다. IMF는 적어도 5년 동안은 재역전이 없으리라고 본다. 우쭐대기 쉬울 때가 가장 위험할 수 있다.(매경, 칼럼)   3. ‘만병의 근원’ 미세 염증 → 노화, 비만 등이 가장 큰 원인, 50대에 본격화. 일반적인 건강검진에서 미세 염증을 알 수 없다. 우리가 받는 검사지의 염증 수치는 대체로 급성 염증과 관련이 있다. 운동, 채소, 유익균 등 우리가 아는 건강 수칙 대부분이 미세 염증을 줄이는 데 효과가 있다.(동아)▼  4. 일제시대, 아리랑은 금지곡 → 100년 전인 1926년 10월 1일, 나운규 감독의 영화 ‘아리랑’이 개봉되고 주제곡 아리랑이 크게 불리자 총독부는 1929년 '아리랑'을 금지곡으로 지정했다. '아리랑'은 우리가 2012년, 북한은 2014년에 각각 유네스코 무형문화유산으로 등록했다.(한경)  5. K드라마, 영화, 재주는 곰이 넘고 돈은 다른 사람이... → 제작사 대표 김모씨, ‘해외에서 1위를 해도 우리가 받는 건 제작비에 마진 10%를 얹은 게 전부’ 밝혀. K팝은 아이돌에 대한 주도권을 국내 기획사가 쥐었지만 영화·드라마는 아직 그러지 못하다는 평가.(중앙선데이)▼   6. 빅테크 거부들, ‘부유세’ 피해 캘리포니아 탈출? → 자산 10억 달러(약 1조4,000억 원) 넘는 부호들에게 일회성으로 자산의 5%를 세금으로 걷는 주민제안 내달 투표. 자산 350조 구글 창업자 등 10여명 벌써 주소 옮겨... 마크 저커버그는 현재 잔류, 젠슨 황은 잔류 공개 선언.(한국)  7. ‘정시 20%’ vs ‘수시 80%’... 이게 맞나? → 대입을 겪기 전이라면 흔히 수능만 잘 보면 되는 줄 안다. 아니다. 현재 대입에서 정시 모집은 20%에 불과하다. 그러나 한국교육개발원의 조사에선 ‘대입에 가장 많이 반영되어야 할 항목’으로 수능은 29.3%로 1위를 기록한 반면 내신은 18.8%로 4위에 그쳤다. 입시 관련 기사의 댓글에서 가장 많이 추천을 받는 글 또한 ‘정시 비중을 예전처럼 늘려야 한다’다.(서울경제)  8. 숫자 8자리, 16자리 비밀번호의 차이 → 숫자 8자리 비밀번호의 조합은 1억개다. 가장 흔한 해킹 방법은 일일이 대입해 보는 거다. 다 대입해 보는데 최신 그래픽카드로 15분이 걸린다. 그러나 16자리 비밀번호는 2배가 아닌 3000년이 걸린다.(한경)  9. 히잡 쓰지 말라는 정부 vs 히잡 쓰겠다는 국민 → 아제르바이잔 정부가 학교 내에서 히잡 사용을 금지하는 정책을 시행하자 학생, 학부모 반발 시위 확산. 집권당은 ‘소녀들이 히잡을 쓰는 것은 어른들의 권유 때문’이라며 해당 정책을 계속 한다는 입장.(국민)  10. ‘홀몸도 아닌데 여기 앉아요’는 큰 실례 → 임신부에게 자리를 양보할 때 흔히 쓸 수 있는 말이지만 큰 실례가 되는 말이다. ‘홀몸’은 ‘배우자나 형제가 없는 사람’을 말한다. 이럴 때는 ‘홑몸’(=아이를 배지 아니한 몸)이 맞다.(한국, ‘우리말 한 자밤’)

𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐈𝐅𝐘𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐀 𝐅𝐈𝐋𝐄’𝐒 𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐄𝐆𝐑𝐈𝐓𝐘 𝐈𝐒 𝐍𝐎𝐓 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐒𝐀𝐌𝐄 𝐀𝐒 𝐏𝐑𝐎𝐕𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐈𝐓 𝐈𝐒 𝐒𝐀𝐅𝐄. 🛡️  Distributed file-sharing systems need mechanisms to detect corrupted or altered data.  BitTorrent uses integrity-checking mechanisms so clients can verify downloaded pieces against the expected information defined by the relevant torrent format.  This helps establish that received pieces match the content description being used.  But there is an important limitation.  A file can be transferred exactly as described and still contain malware, misleading information, or unwanted software.  Integrity verification answers a question about whether the data matches its expected representation. It does not automatically establish whether the content is trustworthy or safe to execute.  This distinction matters across all distributed systems.  A cryptographic hash can help detect changes, but if the original source is malicious, verifying the hash does not make the content benign.  Users should therefore consider the source’s reputation, file type, expected content, and appropriate security checks before opening or executing downloaded material.  For developers building distributed applications, integrity checks should be combined with appropriate trust and validation mechanisms.  The BTT ecosystem’s broader connection to decentralized resource coordination does not remove the need for these foundational protections.  The technical lesson is simple: data integrity, authenticity, and safety are separate properties.  A secure system should understand each one rather than assuming that a successful download proves everything that matters.  @justinsuntron #TRONEcoStar @BitTorrent

2/2:  If acknowledging that AI has become astonishingly capable threatens my identity, my mind has an incentive to find reasons the evidence must be exaggerated, illegitimate, aesthetically inferior, “not real mathematics,” missing some ineffable quality, or otherwise not count.  But if my worth survives either conclusion, I can investigate much more freely.  Maybe the models really are transformative. Maybe their limitations are being underestimated. Maybe mathematicians retain crucial advantages. Maybe the profession changes beyond recognition. Maybe entirely new forms of mathematical work emerge.  I can afford to find out, because the answer is no longer deciding whether I still deserve to respect myself.  That, to me, is one of the deepest human-capital problems AI is revealing.  We spent centuries teaching people how to become valuable through mastery.  We spent far less time teaching them how to remain psychologically secure when mastery stops being scarce.  And as AI reaches more prestigious cognitive professions, that missing skill is going to matter far beyond mathematics.  The loom worker, switchboard operator, factory worker, translator, programmer, lawyer, physician, researcher, artist, and mathematician may differ enormously in social status, but there is a common human vulnerability underneath technological displacement:  If you build your identity around the proposition “this is what makes me somebody,” eventually history may ask what happens when this changes.  It would be far kinder—and probably far better for adaptation, truth-seeking, and innovation—if people learned how to answer that question before history asks it for them.

7/7 My #NeuroP5 framework (power, profit, pleasure, pride and permanency) highlights the diverse motivations shaping how actors pursue and exercise power.  Combined with #SymbioticRealism’s account of the animus dominandi, it helps explain why appeals to restraint alone are insufficient.  Sustainable #NearParity requires rules, incentives and safeguards that make cooperation compatible with competing strategic and institutional interests. The Cold War experience demonstrates that reciprocal vulnerability can help constrain direct confrontation, but also that stability remains fragile without communication, negotiated limits and responsible behaviour.  Near-parity is neither a guarantee of peace nor a substitute for diplomacy. It is a strategic condition that can make unilateral coercion more difficult and reciprocal restraint more attractive.  The central challenge in the #AI and #SpaceRace is therefore not to achieve absolute dominance, but to manage asymmetries, preserve reciprocal constraints and keep technological competition compatible with non-conflictual cooperation and the long-term collective security of humanity. Global power is no longer measured by military strength alone. It is also measured by what a country can deny others access to.  Iran has the Strait of Hormuz. China has critical minerals and magnets. The United States has the dollar and its influence over global payment systems. These are economic chokepoints strategic pressure points that can be used to influence other nations.  But weaponising economic interdependence comes with a cost. Countries respond by building alternative pipelines, diversifying mineral supplies and reducing their dependence on the dollar.  The geopolitical lesson for Africa is clear: dependence can become a vulnerability. Nations that rely heavily on external powers for energy, strategic resources, finance and critical infrastructure risk losing room to manoeuvre when those relationships become instruments of pressure.  The real contest is not just over who controls the chokepoints, but who can build alternatives before that control is used against them.  Geopolitics with Oladimeji Bolarinwa

딥시크 안 써도 걸린다는 지침의 한 줄  딥시크를 직접 안 써도 걸린다. 미국 정부가 이번에 그어놓은 선이 바로 이거다.  19일(현지시간) 미 국토안보부가 연방 관보에 지침을 올렸다는 기사를 읽다가 스크롤이 멈췄다. 연방 기관은 IT 시스템에서 딥시크 AI 에이전트를 빼야 하고, 딥시크 모델 사용은 전면 금지. 여기까진 예상했다.  문제는 다음 줄이다. 딥시크를 기반으로 만든 제삼자 서비스도 도입이 금지된다. 앞으로 딥시크는 연방정부 계약에도 참여할 수 없다.  이유로 든 건 '다중 보안 위협 경로'. 정부 직원이나 납품 업체가 쓰면 민감한 데이터가 중국으로 넘어갈 위험이 있고, 악성코드나 보안 취약점 가능성도 있다고 했다. 이건 어디까지나 국토안보부의 설명이고, 기사에 구체적인 증거까지는 안 나온다. 상무부와 해군 같은 곳은 이미 업무용 기기에서 먼저 뺐다고 한다.  결과부터 말하면, 이번 지침의 무게는 모델 이름이 아니라 '그 모델 위에 올라탄 서비스'까지 막았다는 데 있다고 본다. 내가 쓰는 앱이 속에서 어느 모델을 돌리는지 모르면, 쓰는 사람도 같이 걸릴 수 있다는 얘기니까.  퇴근하고 혼자 이것저것 만드는 사람 기준으로, 나는 이번 주에 이렇게 해볼 생각이다.  1. 내 스크립트와 앱이 부르는 AI를 전부 적어본다. 모델 이름, 어느 회사 API인지, 중간에 끼는 중개 서비스까지. 적다 보면 이거 뭐 쓰는 거였지 싶은 게 꼭 나온다.  2. 무료 챗봇이나 중개 앱은 설정이나 약관에서 속 모델이 뭔지 찾아본다. 안 적혀 있으면 민감한 건 아예 안 넣는다.  3. 고객 정보, 회사 파일, API 키는 어떤 모델에도 통째로 붙여넣지 않는다. 딥시크라서가 아니라 어디든 마찬가지다.  4. 모델 이름을 코드 안에 박아두지 말고 설정 파일 한 줄로 뺀다. 갈아끼워야 하는 날 10분이면 끝난다.  쓰는 도구의 속을 모르면, 금지가 걸리는 날 내 작업도 같이 멈춘다.  지금 쓰는 AI 앱이 속에서 어느 모델로 돌아가는지 확인해본 사람 있나? 어디서 찾았는지, 아니면 못 찾았는지 궁금하다.  출처: 헤럴드경제 — 트럼프, 美 정부서 딥시크 전면 퇴출[1일1트]

이제 통신망도 국가안보다. 미국은 왜 파이브 아이즈를 움직이는가?  FIVE EYES SECURE COMMUNICATION NETWORKS  조금 전 우크라이나의 Starlink·Starshield 통신 제한을 통해 현대전에서 연결망이 얼마나 중요한지 살펴봤습니다.  이번에는 미국 FCC가 영국·캐나다·호주·뉴질랜드와 함께 통신망 보안과 공급망 보호를 위한 협력을 강화한다고 발표했습니다.  저는 두 사건을 연결해서 바라볼 필요가 있다고 생각합니다.  현대전에서는 무기를 확보하는 것만큼 그 무기를 연결하는 통신망을 보호하는 능력이 중요해지고 있습니다.  이번 회의에서는 통신장비 공급망, 사이버 공격 대응, 핵심 통신 인프라의 복원력 등이 논의됐습니다.  물론 이번 발표가 우크라이나 사태의 직접적인 대응책이라는 의미는 아닙니다.  그러나 정책의 방향은 분명해 보입니다.  통신망은 더 이상 단순한 상업 인프라가 아니라 국가안보와 경제안보를 지탱하는 전략적 자산입니다.  앞으로는 통신기술의 성능뿐 아니라 보안, 공급망의 신뢰성, 서비스 지속성, 위기 상황에서의 통제권이 더욱 중요해질 것입니다.  저는 이제 한 가지를 더 지켜보려 합니다.  이러한 협력이 실제 규제와 정부 조달, 그리고 독립적이고 복원력 있는 통신망 구축으로 얼마나 이어질 것인가.  앞선 아티클의 질문을 다시 떠올려 봅니다.  전쟁을 움직이는 것이 연결망이라면, 그 연결망을 누가 통제하고 지킬 것인가?  FCC — 공식 X 원 게시글 nitter.mie.foundation/FCC/status/21111430833…  ※ 본 글은 공개자료를 바탕으로 확인된 사실과 분석·전망을 구분해 작성했습니다. 특정 종목의 매수·매도 권유가 아닙니다.

sample_tweets.text: DHS(미국 국토안보부)가 감시하고 있습니다: 권위에 의문을 제기하면, 당신은 극단주의자로 낙인찍힐 수 있습니다. 퓨전 센터와 감시 네트워크가 당신을 주시하고 있습니다.  미국 국토안보부는 9.11 테러 이후 외부 위협 방지에서, 권위에 의문을 제기하는 비판적 사고를 하는 사람들을 극단주의자로 규정하는 내부 시스템으로 전환했습니다. 선거의 공정성을 문제 삼거나, 정부의 명령에 반대하거나, 공식적인 설명을 검토하는 시민들은 퓨전 센터, CISA(사이버 보안 및 인프라 보안국), 그리고 알버트 센서를 통해 감시를 받습니다. 이 네트워크는 2026년 가을에도 계속 운영될 예정입니다.  9.11 테러 이후 외국 위협에 대응하기 위해 설립된 DHS는 보안 문제를 명분으로 관료 조직으로 확장되었습니다. 일반 미국 시민을 잠재적인 위협으로 규정하면서, DHS의 관심은 내부로 향하게 되었습니다.  퓨전 센터는 연방, 주, 지방 정부 기관들을 연결합니다. 이들은 시민들을 감시하는 허브 역할을 하며, 보고에 따르면 실시간 선거 데이터를 수집하여, 선거 과정을 통제할 수 있는 위치에 있습니다. 2026년 말의 보고서에 따르면, 데이터 파이프라인을 통해 정보가 퓨전 센터와 DHS 데이터베이스로 전송됩니다.  알버트 센서는 인터넷 보안 센터에서 관리하며, 중요한 기반 시설을 위한 도구로 제시됩니다. 이 장치들은 네트워크 트래픽을 감시하며, 선거 데이터가 투명한 감독 없이 퓨전 센터에 전달될 수 있다는 우려를 낳고 있습니다. 이 연결은 크래들포인트 라우터를 통해 이루어지며, 이 라우터 중 상당수가 중국에서 제조되어, 보안 취약점이 존재할 가능성에 대한 의문을 제기합니다.  CISA는 조정 역할을 수행합니다. 크리스 크레브스와 같은 인물과 관련되어 있으며, 소셜 미디어를 감시하고, 반대 의견을 허위 정보로 규정하며, 인터넷 보안 센터와 협력하고 있습니다. MS-ISAC 및 EL-ISAC 그룹은 지방 정부, 연방 기관, 그리고 계약업체들 간에 민감한 데이터를 공유합니다.  최근 DHS의 보고서에 따르면, 선거 결과를 의문을 제기하거나, 특정 정책에 반대하거나, 정부의 권한 확장에 저항하는 개인들이 극단주의자 목록에 포함되었습니다. 2026년 11월 중간 선거가 다가옴에 따라, 이러한 시스템은 계속 운영될 것입니다.  소규모 정부 지지자들은 점진적인 개혁으로는 충분하지 않다고 주장합니다. 그들은 퓨전 센터를 폐지하고, CISA 및 관련 센터를 폐지하거나 대폭 제한하며, 알버트 센서와 중국산 라우터에 대한 의존도를 줄이고, 남은 기능에 대한 엄격한 공공 감시를 도입할 것을 제안합니다.  내부 감시는 자유를 훼손합니다. 독립적인 사고를 중시하고, 공식적인 설명을 계속 의문을 제기하는 시민들은 감시 대상에 오를 위험이 있습니다. 예산 삭감과 해체를 요구하는 대중의 목소리가 필요합니다.

$PLTR Maven 추가 활동:    Maven은 NATO의 동부 견제 이니셔티브의 중추입니다 :  “지휘소들은 Maven 스마트 시스템을 포함한 차세대 지휘통제 소프트웨어를 활용하여 분산된 국가 본부들 간의 통합된 공통 작전 그림을 구축했습니다.   이 공통 데이터 백본은 군사 계획자들에게 방대한 작전 데이터를 처리하고, 지휘관의 의사결정 주기를 가속화하며, 육상, 공중, 해상, 사이버 및 우주 영역 전반에 걸쳐 심층 화력을 조정할 수 있게 했습니다.”    “10월 6일부터 15일까지 진행된 이번 훈련은 프랑스, 독일, 네덜란드, 폴란드 전역의 지휘소에서 운영되는 약 2,000명의 미국 군인과 2,000명의 다국적 인력을 한자리에 모았습니다.   Avenger Triad 26은 NATO의 최고 수준 지휘소 훈련인 Steadfast Duel 26과 동기화되었으며, 이는 모든 32개 동맹국에 걸친 전략 및 작전 의사결정자들을 연결했습니다.”  “이번 훈련의 핵심 목표는 NATO의 동부 견제 이니셔티브의 개념들을 작전 실천으로 옮기는 것이었습니다.  고정된 방어선에만 의존하는 대신, EFDI는 첨단 센서, 무인 항공 시스템, 클라우드 컴퓨팅, 공유 데이터 환경을 통합하여 위협 탐지와 표적 교전 사이의 시간을 단축합니다.”   “작년 우리는 높은 수준으로 마무리했으며, 올해는 그 수준에서 시작했습니다.”라고 Lowin이 말했습니다.   “우리의 억제력의 신뢰성은 우리의 능력에 달려 있습니다. 적이 32개 국가가 데이터를 원활하게 공유하고, 수천 킬로미터에 걸친 군단급 대형을 지휘하며, 몇 분 만에 합동 화력을 조정할 수 있다는 것을 알게 되면, 이는 명백한 신호를 보냅니다 :   NATO를 공격하는 것은 성공하지 못할 것입니다.”

🚨속보  JP모건 CEO "미국 경제는 호황…하지만 위험은 커지고 있다"  JP모건의 제이미 다이먼 CEO는 월스트리트저널 인터뷰에서,  - 미국 경제가 기업 이익 급증과 낮은 실업률에 힘입어 호황을 누리고 있지만, 막대한 재정적자와 인플레이션, 지정학적 갈등과 사이버 공격이 주요 위험 요인이라고 평가  - 특히 AI 투자는 경제 성장을 뒷받침하고 있지만, 데이터센터 건설 등 대규모 지출이 단기적으로 인플레이션을 자극할 수 있다.  - 또한 경기 침체가 언제 찾아올지는 예측할 수 없다며, JP모건은 주식시장이 40% 급락하거나 신용 스프레드가 2~3배 벌어지는 상황까지 대비하고 있다.  - 사이버 공격에 대해서는 "지금은 단연 최대 리스크"라며, 광케이블과 수도·교통 등 보안이 취약한 핵심 인프라를 우려했고, 기업들이 당장 네트워크 분리와 보안 취약점의 신속한 보완에 나서야 한다.

초등학교 때는 구구단조차 제대로 못 외우고 기초 숙제는 백지로 내면서도 조금만 공부를 열심히 하면 서울대를 넘어 하버드 스탠퍼드라도 갈 수 있을 거 같이 생각들을 하는 어린이들이 가끔 있고, 어릴 땐 그런 근자감이 귀엽기도 하다. 하지만 나이도 먹을 만큼 먹고 현실감을 찾아야 할 시기가 지났음에도 그런 소리를 하고 있으면 조롱당하거나 외면당하는 수밖에 더 있나. 지금 전시작전통제권 조기 환수를 부르짖는 이재명의 안보관이 딱 이 모양이다.  국가의 군사 주권을 논하고 연합군을 지휘하겠다는 거창한 포부를 밝히기 전에, 이 나라의 가장 기본적인 보안 숙제가 어떻게 돌아가고 있는지 성적표부터 까보자.  국가정보원이 이미 2021년 12월에 중국 제조사 클라우드와 자동으로 통신이 가능하다며 긴급 보안 조치를 요구했던 중국산 위장 CCTV가 있다. 납품 업체 대표는 대외무역법 위반과 사기 혐의로 징역 4년 형이 대법원에서 확정되기까지 했다. 백도어가 심어져 있어 국가 기밀이 중국 서버로 실시간 전송될 수 있다는 뜻이다.  그런데 이 범죄 판결이 난 스파이 카메라가 지금 어디에 달려 있는가. 국가 최고 보안 등급인 가급 중요시설, 인천 LNG 기지 내부 감시용으로 16대가 버젓이 돌아가고 있다. 한국가스공사 전체로 넓히면 무려 243대, 한국석유공사 비축기지에는 261대가 깔려 있다. 더 기가 막힌 것은 국정원의 시정 통보를 받고도 가스공사가 이 중국산 위장 모델을 91대나 추가로 구매해 달았다는 사실이다.  국가 에너지 동맥의 눈과 귀를 베이징의 클라우드 서버에 자발적으로 상납해 놓고, 수년째 전선 하나 뽑지 못하는 처참한 꼬라지다. 방구석에 앉아 기사를 읽는 내 눈에도 이토록 가소롭고 한심해 보이는데, 세계 최강의 정보력을 굴리는 미국의 눈에는 이 나라의 보안 수준이 대체 어떻게 비치겠는가.  안방 문짝이 중국 해커들에게 통째로 뜯겨 나간 이 판국에, 청와대 춘추관에 앉아 트윗질이나 하는 이재명은 전작권을 반드시 조기에 환수해야 하고 충분히 그럴 능력이 있다며 기염을 토했다. 기초적인 문단속조차 못 해 중국에 국가 기간시설을 생중계해 주는 주제에 미군의 첨단 전략 자산을 지휘하겠다고 손을 내미니, 미국이 대북 정보 공유를 제한하고 한미일 사이버 안보 회의에서 국정원을 패싱하며 문전박대하는 것이 당연지사 아닌가.  여기에 더해 북한의 핵무기를 최후 방어무기라고 진단한 대목에 이르면 헛웃음만 터져 나온다. 북한 핵이 최후 방어용이라니, 대한민국 대통령이 대놓고 평양의 수석 대변인 같은 소리를 하고 있지 않은가. 수천만 국민의 머리 위에 매달린 실존적 학살 무기를 두고, 김정은 정권의 체제 수호 논리를 토씨 하나 안 틀리고 그대로 읊어대며 정당성을 부여해 주었다.  주적의 핵무기에는 이토록 자애로운 변명을 늘어놓으면서 동맹국을 향해서는 당장 작전통제권을 내놓으라고 핏대를 세우니, 미국 입장에서 참으로 믿음직스러워 깨나 전작권을 넘겨주고 싶겠다. 미군 수뇌부가 바보 천치가 아닌 이상, 북한 대변인 노릇을 하는 자에게 자국 장병들의 목숨과 핵우산의 열쇠를 맡길 리가 있겠는가.  낭만적인 좌파식 망상에 빠져 동맹의 지휘 체계를 흔들기 전에, 당장 인천 LNG 기지와 석유 비축기지에 매달린 중국산 카메라부터 떼어내는 기초 숙제나 똑바로 하시라. 앞문으로는 북한의 핵보유를 방어용이라 감싸주고 뒷문으로는 중국에 국가 기간망을 열어주면서 입으로만 외치는 자주국방은, 안보를 빙자한 자해 공갈에 불과하다. 서울대 타령은 제발 한글부터 떼고 하시길 바란다.
보안 패치를 위한 오픈웨이트 사이버 모델. 당장 써봐야죠.
